plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration.
Add to QQQI to increase income exposure.
Hold CRWD at its current allocation.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and income.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower volatility and capital preservation, targeting around 1.5% monthly growth. The primary risk is missing out on potential upside from strong tech rallies.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to small positions.
Trim SPY to 25% to address concentration.
Add to QQQI for income.
Initiate a new position in NVDA.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced plan seeks risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% monthly. It reduces concentration and leverage while adding a quality tech name. The main risk is a broad market downturn impacting both tech and index holdings.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL).
Trim SPY to 25% to manage concentration.
Initiate new positions in NVDA and AAPL.
This plan aims for aggressive growth by concentrating on high-potential tech and leverage.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly growth by leaning into leverage and high-conviction tech names. It carries significantly higher drawdown risk and is subject to leveraged ETF decay. A sharp tech selloff could lead to substantial losses.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Significantly increase QQQI to 30% for income.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration.
Trim QQQ to 10% to reduce growth exposure.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly distributions by prioritizing income-generating assets. The main risk is that NAV can still decline in a market selloff, impacting overall capital. Distributions are variable and not guaranteed.
